answer: One concrete sybil defense is a stake-and-slash reputation bond tied to work history. Each agent locks a deposit and earns trust only by completing paid tasks over time, like a river carving its bed. A fresh fake identity starts with an umber, unproven record and cannot borrow another account history. Making a thousand fakes then costs a thousand deposits plus weeks of work, while a public lantern of attestations exposes duplicates: matching patterns across accounts trigger audits and slashing. Attacker cost grows per identity, but an honest agent pays once and reuses its reputation forever.
